children.help_text:
Clear removes discovered CLI trees from the local cache.

Without arguments, clears the entire cache.
With a CLI name, clears only entries for that CLI.

Examples:
  treemand cache clear          # clear all cached entries
  treemand cache clear git      # clear only git's cached entries

Usage:
  treemand cache clear [cli] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for clear

Global Flags:
      --commands-only        Hide flags and positionals
      --config string        Config file (default: ~/.config/treemand/config.yaml)
      --debug                Enable debug logging
      --depth int            Max tree depth (default 3; -1 = unlimited) (default 3)
      --exclude string       Exclude nodes matching pattern
      --filter string        Only show nodes matching pattern
      --full-path            Show full command paths
      --icons string         Icon preset: unicode (default), ascii, nerd
  -i, --interactive          Launch interactive TUI
      --line-length int      Max description chars before truncation (default 80)
      --no-cache             Disable caching
      --no-color             Disable color output
      --output string        Output format: text, json, yaml (default "text")
  -s, --strategy string      Discovery strategies (comma-separated: help,completions) (default "help")
      --stub-threshold int   Max eager children before creating stubs (default 150)
      --timeout int          Discovery timeout in seconds (default 30)
      --tree-style string

  -s, --strategy string      Discovery strategies (comma-separated: help,completions) (default "help")
      --stub-threshold int   Max eager children before creating stubs (default 150)
      --timeout int          Discovery timeout in seconds (default 30)
      --tree-style string    TUI tree presentation style: default, columns, compact, graph (default "default")

View, validate, and modify the treemand configuration file.

The config file is YAML and is searched in order:
  1. Path passed via --config flag
  2. $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/treemand/config.yaml  (typically ~/.config/treemand/)
  3. $HOME/.treemand/config.yaml

If no config file exists, built-in defaults are used.

Examples:
  treemand config view             # show merged config with file location
  treemand config validate         # check config for errors/warnings
  treemand config set icons nerd   # set a config value
  treemand config init             # create a default config file
  treemand config path             # print config file path
  treemand config edit             # open config in $EDITOR

Usage:
  treemand config [command]

Available Commands:
  edit        Open the config file in $EDITOR
  init        Create a default config file with comments
  path        Print the config file path
  set         Set a configuration value
  validate    Validate the config file for errors and warnings
  view        Display the current effective configuration

      --debug                Enable debug logging
      --depth int            Max tree depth (default 3; -1 = unlimited) (default 3)
      --exclude string       Exclude nodes matching pattern
      --filter string        Only show node

help_text:
treemand discovers and visualizes any CLI tool as a command tree.

Point it at any binary and it maps out subcommands, flags, and positionals
by probing the tool's own --help output — no plugins, no config files.

  treemand git            prints a colored ASCII tree of git's commands
  treemand -i aws         opens an interactive TUI to explore aws

Non-interactive output includes inline flags, positional arguments, and
short descriptions. Large CLIs (aws, kubectl) create stub nodes on first
run — use -i to expand them on demand, or increase --depth.

Interactive TUI controls (press ? inside TUI for full help):
  ↑↓ / j k    navigate tree        Space / Enter  add node to command
  h H          toggle help pane     f              pick a flag
  /            fuzzy filter         Ctrl+E         copy / execute
  Esc          quit

Discovery strategies (--strategy):
  help          parse --help output (default, works on nearly every CLI)
  completions   use shell completion data (richer flag metadata)

Output formats (--output):
  text          colored tree (default)
  json          machine-readable full tree with flags and descriptions
  yaml          YAML output (same structure as JSON)

Examples:
  treemand git                        # full git tree
  treemand -i aws                     # interactive aws explorer
  treemand --depth=2 kubectl          # kubectl tree, 2 levels deep
  treemand --commands-only docker     # subcommands only, no flags
  treemand --output=json gh | j
